fish.name: Dock Gudgeon
fish.flavor: Loiters under the pier like it's waiting for a ferry it has no intention of boarding. Bites anything once, out of civic duty.

fish.name: Pier Smelt
fish.flavor: Smells faintly of cucumber and low tide. Locals insist that's a compliment.

fish.name: Canal Roach
fish.flavor: Eats bread crusts, bottle corks, and the occasional civic notice. Considers itself very well informed.

fish.name: Harbor Herring
fish.flavor: Travels in dense silver crowds, like commuters, and with roughly the same expression.

fish.name: Rope Blenny
fish.flavor: Lives inside coiled mooring rope and defends it like a rent-controlled flat. Will glare at you from a knot.

fish.name: Mudflat Goby
fish.flavor: Sits on the low-tide mud with the smug patience of someone who owns the mud.

fish.name: Bilge Minnow
fish.flavor: Thrives in water that technically shouldn't support life. Nobody has told it, and at this point nobody's going to.

fish.name: Cobblestone Dace
fish.flavor: Its speckles match the canal bottom so exactly that pedestrians occasionally apologize to it.

fish.name: Lamplight Sprat
fish.flavor: Gathers in the streetlamp reflections each night, mistaking them for a warmer, kinder moon. Honestly, who could blame it.

fish.name: Gullbait Sardine
fish.flavor: Named by the gulls, who consider it less a species and more a snack subscription.

fish.name: Tarpaper Flounder
fish.flavor: Flat, gray, and gritty, like the roof of the bait shop. Surprisingly tender, if you ask it nicely.

fish.name: Brackish Perch
fish.flavor: Can't decide between river and sea, so it settled in the harbor and complains about both.

fish.name: Piling Nibbler
fish.flavor: Gnaws barnacles off the dock pilings all day, every day. The harbormaster quietly considers it staff.

fish.name: Ferry Chub
fish.flavor: Follows the ferry back and forth from open to close. It doesn't need to go anywhere; it just likes having a routine.

fish.name: Streetlamp Mullet
fish.flavor: Leaps through the lamplit reflections at dusk. Old dockhands say every splash is a streetlamp making a wish.

fish.name: Harbormaster's Bream
fish.flavor: Wears its scales like brass buttons on a uniform and insists on inspecting every hull it passes. Nobody appointed it. Nobody dares un-appoint it.

fish.name: Rust Eel
fish.flavor: The exact color and temperament of a sunken bicycle. May, at some point, have been a sunken bicycle.

fish.name: Fishwife's Whiting
fish.flavor: The honest, dependable catch that built this town — or at least paid for most of its gossip.

fish.name: Penny Wrasse
fish.flavor: Its scales gleam like the wish-coins scattered on the canal bed. Landing one is legally considered making change.

fish.name: Tollbooth Carp
fish.flavor: Stations itself under the canal bridge and glares meaningfully at every passing boat. No one has ever paid it, but it remains hopeful.

fish.name: Nightwatch Catfish
fish.flavor: Patrols the harbor bottom from dusk till dawn without fail. Whatever it's guarding down there, it takes the job very seriously.

fish.name: Regatta Garfish
fish.flavor: Races the sailboats every summer and, by its own accounting, has never once lost.

fish.name: Cannery Shad
fish.flavor: Its great-grandmother escaped the cannery through a drainpipe in '52. The family still doesn't talk about tins.

fish.name: Brasswhisker Barbel
fish.flavor: Its whiskers gleam like polished doorknockers. Old-timers on the quay tip their hats to it, just in case it turns out to be someone important.

fish.name: Lockkeeper's Pike
fish.flavor: Haunts the canal lock and opens its jaws with the same long groan as the gates. Some say it learned the sound from the hinges; the hinges decline to comment.

fish.name: Foghorn Drum
fish.flavor: On thick nights its booming call rolls across the water, and ships change course out of politeness. The lighthouse keeper considers it a colleague.

fish.name: Wishing-Well Koi
fish.flavor: Escaped a courtyard fountain years ago, and every coin ever tossed at it somehow stuck. It carries a modest fortune in other people's hopes and has no plans to spend it.

fish.name: Lantern Eel
fish.flavor: Glows the precise amber of the quayside gaslamps. The lamplighter counts it on his evening rounds — number thirty-one, the wet one.

fish.name: Mooring-Chain Loach
fish.flavor: Coils around the anchor chains and rusts in quiet sympathy. Sailors who haul one up apologize and lower it gently back down.

fish.name: The Ferryman's Fare
fish.flavor: A pale fish with a single cold coin lodged in its mouth, minted in no currency the bank recognizes. Nobody remembers paying it, and it never offers change.

fish.name: Gaslight Gulper
fish.flavor: Every so often a streetlamp's reflection vanishes from the canal with a soft glup. The city council budgets for replacement reflections quarterly.

fish.name: The Nine O'Clock Toll
fish.flavor: At exactly nine each evening, something beneath the harbor rings like a drowned church bell, and the whole town checks its watches. It is extremely punctual and, on the evidence of one blurry photograph, extremely a fish.

fish.name: Old Barnacle-Beard
fish.flavor: Every angler in town has hooked him exactly once, and every story ends the same way: a snapped line, one slow ripple, and a week of respectful silence. He was old when the harbor was a sandbar with ambitions.

fish.name: The Widow's Lantern
fish.flavor: A soft golden light that drifts the canals on still nights, pausing beneath the windows of those who wait for ships. In three hundred years it has never once been early, and never once failed to come.

fish.name: The City Beneath
fish.flavor: When it rises, the water shows rooftops, streetlamps, and washing lines that the town above has never built. Those who look too long swear they can hear their own doorbells ringing, far below, and someone patiently answering.
